subject: ela
intro: Each item gives you a short presentation scenario. You will pick the claim, spot an off-topic detail, name a weak delivery feature, or choose the next logical point. Everything you need is in the prompt.

items.prompt: Read this part of a presentation: 'Our school should add a garden club. A garden teaches students how plants grow and gives them fresh vegetables to share.' Which sentence states the claim, the main point the speaker wants the audience to accept?
items.answer: The first sentence: 'Our school should add a garden club.'

steps: A claim is the main position the speaker wants the audience to accept, not a fact that backs it up.
The first sentence states what the school should do, so it is the claim.
The second sentence gives reasons that support the claim, so it is a supporting detail, not the claim.

items.prompt: A speaker is presenting the claim 'Our town needs more bike lanes.' Read the supporting points: (1) 'Two cyclists were hurt on Oak Street last year.' (2) 'A survey found most residents would bike more if lanes were safer.' (3) 'My cousin has a really fast mountain bike.' Which detail is off topic and should be cut?
items.answer: Point 3: 'My cousin has a really fast mountain bike.'

steps: Each supporting detail should give a reason the town needs more bike lanes.
Points 1 and 2 show that biking is unsafe now and that people would bike more with safer lanes.
Point 3 only mentions one person's bike. It shares the word 'bike' but does not support the need for lanes, so it should be cut.

items.prompt: Read this description of a presentation: 'Marcus read in such a quiet voice that students in the back row said they could not hear a single word.' Which delivery feature most needs improvement?
items.answer: Volume. Marcus needs to speak louder so the whole audience can hear.

steps: Delivery features include volume, eye contact, and clear pronunciation.
The problem is that listeners could not hear him because his voice was too quiet.
Speaking too quietly is a volume problem, so volume is the feature that needs improvement.

items.prompt: Read this part of a presentation: 'Recess should be longer. A study of grade schools found that students who got more recess paid better attention in class.' Which sentence provides the supporting findings, the facts and details that back up the claim?
items.answer: The second sentence: 'A study of grade schools found that students who got more recess paid better attention in class.'

steps: The supporting findings are the facts and details that back up the main point.
The first sentence states the claim that recess should be longer.
The second sentence reports a study, which is a fact that supports the claim, so it provides the findings.

items.prompt: Read this description of a presentation: 'During her whole talk, Jada stared down at her note cards and never once looked up at the people listening.' Which delivery feature most needs improvement?
items.answer: Eye contact. Jada needs to look up at the audience instead of staring at her note cards.

steps: Delivery features include volume, eye contact, and clear pronunciation.
Jada looked only at her note cards and never looked at the audience.
Looking at the audience is eye contact, so eye contact is the feature she needs to improve.

items.prompt: A student is presenting the claim 'School lunches should include more fresh fruit.' Read the supporting points: (1) 'The school nurse said only one fruit option is offered on most days.' (2) 'Doctors recommend eating fruit every day.' (3) 'I do not like the cafeteria pizza.' Which detail is off topic and should be cut?
items.answer: Point 3: 'I do not like the cafeteria pizza.'

steps: Each detail should support the claim that lunches need more fresh fruit.
Points 1 and 2 give a fact about the current options and a reason fruit matters.
Point 3 is a personal opinion about pizza and does not support adding fruit, so it should be cut.

items.prompt: Read this part of a presentation: 'Students should be allowed to bring water bottles to class. Staying hydrated helps the brain focus during long lessons.' Which sentence states the claim, the main point the speaker wants the audience to accept?
items.answer: The first sentence: 'Students should be allowed to bring water bottles to class.'

steps: The claim is the main position the speaker wants the audience to accept.
The first sentence says what students should be allowed to do, so it is the claim.
The second sentence gives a reason that supports the claim, so it is a supporting detail.

items.prompt: A student wants to present these three points in a logical order: (1) 'Here is my plan for a class recycling bin.' (2) 'Our class should recycle its paper.' (3) 'We throw away a full bin of paper every week.' Which point should come first to begin the presentation?
items.answer: Point 2: 'Our class should recycle its paper.'

steps: A presentation usually begins by stating the claim, then shows the problem, then gives the plan.
Point 2 is the claim, so it should come first.
Point 3 shows the problem and point 1 gives the plan, so they come after the claim.

items.prompt: Read this description of a presentation: 'Liam mumbled his words so much that the audience could not tell whether he said fifteen or fifty.' Which delivery feature most needs improvement?
items.answer: Clear pronunciation. Liam needs to say his words clearly so the audience can understand each one.

steps: Delivery features include volume, eye contact, and clear pronunciation.
Liam mumbled, so the audience could not tell his words apart.
Mumbling is a pronunciation problem, so clear pronunciation is the feature he needs to improve.

items.prompt: A speaker is presenting the claim 'Our class should take a field trip to the science museum.' Read the supporting points: (1) 'The museum has a new exhibit on the planets we are studying.' (2) 'Field trips help students remember lessons better.' (3) 'My family went to the beach last summer.' Which detail is off topic and should be cut?
items.answer: Point 3: 'My family went to the beach last summer.'

steps: Each detail should support taking a field trip to the science museum.
Points 1 and 2 connect the museum to what the class studies and explain why trips help.
Point 3 is about a beach trip and has nothing to do with the science museum, so it should be cut.

items.prompt: Read this part of a presentation: 'Our school day should start later. Doctors report that teens who sleep longer feel less tired and learn more.' Which sentence states the claim, the main point the speaker wants the audience to accept?
items.answer: The first sentence: 'Our school day should start later.'

steps: The claim is the main position the speaker wants the audience to accept.
The first sentence says the school day should start later, so it is the claim.
The second sentence reports what doctors say, which is a supporting fact, not the claim.

items.prompt: A student wants to present these three points in a logical order: (1) 'Many students skip breakfast and feel hungry by ten.' (2) 'Our school should offer free breakfast.' (3) 'Here is how the cafeteria could serve it each morning.' Which point should come first to begin the presentation?
items.answer: Point 2: 'Our school should offer free breakfast.'

steps: A presentation usually begins with the claim, then the problem, then the plan.
Point 2 states the claim, so it should come first.
Point 1 shows the problem and point 3 gives the plan, so they follow the claim.

items.prompt: A speaker has just stated the claim 'Our class should adopt a class pet.' Which point is the most pertinent supporting detail to say next?
items.answer: A relevant, specific fact such as 'Studies show that caring for a class pet teaches students responsibility.'

steps: After stating a claim, the next point should be a specific detail that supports it.
A fact about how caring for a pet teaches responsibility directly supports adopting a class pet.
A personal opinion or an unrelated comment would not support the claim, so the supporting fact is the best next point.

items.prompt: Read this description of a presentation: 'Sam spoke so softly that even the teacher standing right in front of him had to ask him to repeat himself.' Which delivery feature most needs improvement?
items.answer: Volume. Sam needs to speak louder so listeners can hear him.

steps: Delivery features include volume, eye contact, and clear pronunciation.
Sam spoke so softly that he had to be asked to repeat himself.
Speaking too softly is a volume problem, so volume is the feature he needs to improve.

items.prompt: A speaker is presenting the claim 'Our library should stay open later after school.' Read the supporting points: (1) 'Many students said they need a quiet place to study after class.' (2) 'A survey found the library is busiest in the hour before it closes.' (3) 'The new library carpet is blue.' Which detail is off topic and should be cut?
items.answer: Point 3: 'The new library carpet is blue.'

steps: Each detail should support keeping the library open later.
Points 1 and 2 show that students need study time and that the library is busy near closing.
Point 3 describes the carpet color, which does not support longer hours, so it should be cut.
